bull.b: Arm’s licensing and royalty model supports exceptionally high gross margins while generating substantial operating and free cash flow. This combination gives the company resources to fund research, ecosystem expansion and new products without relying heavily on external financing.

Rapid data-center royalty growth and rising Neoverse volumes indicate that Arm is expanding beyond its established mobile position into infrastructure computing. Broader exposure to cloud and AI workloads can create a durable source of royalty growth as customers seek energy-efficient compute.

Major cloud deployments validate Arm’s ecosystem, while the AGI CPU extends the company from processor IP toward more complete AI compute solutions. This can increase customer engagement, broaden revenue opportunities and deepen Arm’s role in future system architectures.

bear.b: Smartphones remain a major royalty market, so weaker handset demand and higher bill-of-material costs can slow chip shipments and Arm’s usage-based revenue. This creates a durable near-term constraint on royalty growth even as data-center demand strengthens.

bear.t: Supply constraints limit AGI CPU ramp
bear.b: The AGI CPU opportunity cannot scale solely through customer demand because production depends on constrained wafer, substrate, testing and memory capacity. These bottlenecks may delay shipments, defer royalty or silicon revenue and limit the pace of strategic expansion.

bear.t: Initial AGI CPU margins are low
bear.b: The initial AGI CPU margin profile is materially below Arm’s established IP economics, creating a transition-period drag if the product becomes a larger revenue contributor. Reaching the targeted margin improvement depends on scale and execution over multiple years.
